items.title: Business development in law firms: How it builds client flow in India and internationally
items.summary: Ask most lawyers what wins a client and you will hear about the excellence of the work. That is only half the story. Before a client can judge the work, someone must introduce the firm, understand the client's problem and keep the relationship alive long after the file is closed. Increasingly, that someone is the business development (BD) team. BD is no longer a side activity for partners with spare time. It is a discipline of its own. This article looks at how BD works within India's advertising restrictions, how firms build visibility, and what it takes to win and keep clients at home and overseas. Why business development matters more than ever Work once reached Indian law firms through reputation and referrals. A founder's name, a few well-known deals and word of mouth did most of the job. That still works, but clients have changed. General counsel and overseas companies now compare firms on how quickly they respond, how clearly they price and how well they understand the business, not just the statute. BD sits in the middle of this. A good team studies the market, prepares pitches, manages directory submissions, and tells the firm which opportunities fit. Working within Rule 3

items.title: Is the Collegium system failing women?
items.summary: Proportional representation is fundamental to a democratic society. The legitimacy of public institutions depends not merely on their independence, but also on whether people from different sections of society have a meaningful opportunity to participate in them. This becomes particularly important in the judiciary, where representation influences not only institutional diversity, but also public confidence in the administration of justice. The persistent underrepresentation of women in India's higher judiciary, therefore, demands serious examination. Recently on October 6, 2026, Justice Sunita Agarwal took oath as a judge of the Supreme Court of India, only the 13th woman to be appointed to the Court in its history. Her appointment increased the number of women judges from two to three, against a working strength of 37 judges. Women, therefore, constitute just 8.1 per cent of the Supreme Court's strength. More than seven decades after its establishment, the country's highest judicial institution continues to have a strikingly poor record of women's representation. items.title: No work, little compensation: Delhi’s construction workers pay the price for its toxic air
items.summary: Delhi’s air pollution worsens every winter, prompting the government to impose restrictions under the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP). These include halting construction work and restricting the entry of certain vehicles. But when construction sites shut down, it is migrant workers who bear the brunt. With no work or alternative source of income, many go weeks, sometimes months, without a wage. Some are forced to return to their villages with their children because they can no longer afford to stay in Delhi. In a November 24, 2021 order, the Supreme Court directed the government to provide financial assistance to workers affected by construction bans. In December 2025, Delhi minister Kapil Mishra announced compensation of Rs 10,000 for workers who lost work due to GRAP restrictions. Newslaundry spoke to construction workers who say they had registered with the Delhi Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board nearly two years ago and renewed their registrations on time, but have still not received the promised compensation. items.title: Ola's extra pay for faster rides feature doesn't work: CCPA asks it to scrap practice, slaps ₹10 lakh penalty
items.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has imposed a penalty of ₹10 lakh on ANI Technologies Private Limited, which operates Ola, for misleading consumers into paying additional amounts to improve their chances of securing a ride. In an order dated November 10, the CCPA held that Ola's practice of prompting customers to pay extra before a driver accepted their booking amounted to a misleading advertisement, unfair trade practice and unfair contract under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019. Hence, it ordered the platform to stop the feature/ practice while also imposing a penalty on it. The order was passed by Chief Commissioner Nidhi Khare and Commissioner Anupam Mishra . The proceedings arose from a complaint received in May 2025 concerning Ola's advance tipping feature. While customers waited for a driver to accept their booking, the app displayed messages suggesting that paying an additional amount could improve their chances of securing a ride. One such prompt stated: "Adding a tip might help increase the chances of getting a ride faster."
